partners.diseaseBName: severe combined immunodeficiency, autosomal recessive, T cell-negative, B cell-negative, NK cell-positive
partners.mechanism_chain: RAG1 (HGNC:9831) —DISRUPTS→ V(D)J recombination (REACT:R-HSA-169968); RAG2 (HGNC:9832) —DISRUPTS→ V(D)J recombination (REACT:R-HSA-169968); V(D)J recombination (REACT:R-HSA-169968) —LEADS_TO→ Severe combined immunodeficiency (HP:0002714); V(D)J recombination (REACT:R-HSA-169968) —LEADS_TO→ Partial RAG1 deficiency (HP:0011418). Loss-of-function mutations in RAG1 or RAG2 disrupt the V(D)J recombination pathway, which is essential for adaptive immune receptor gene rearrangement. This disruption leads to severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID) and, in cases of partial deficiency or specific mutations, can manifest as combined immunodeficiency due to partial RAG1 deficiency.

partners.mechanism_chain: RAG1 (HGNC:9831) —DISRUPTS→ V(D)J recombination (REACT:R-HSA-168974); V(D)J recombination (REACT:R-HSA-168974) —LEADS_TO→ Combined immunodeficiency (HP:0002695); V(D)J recombination (REACT:R-HSA-168974) —LEADS_TO→ Skin granulomas (HP:0030035). Loss-of-function mutations in RAG1 disrupt the V(D)J recombination pathway, which is essential for adaptive immune receptor assembly. This disruption leads to combined immunodeficiency (affecting both T and B cells) in both diseases. In the case of combined immunodeficiency with skin granulomas, the V(D)J recombination defect also manifests with the specific phenotype of skin granulomas.

Strategies aimed at restoring RAG enzyme activity or compensating for its loss could potentially benefit patients with both disease categories.
